meaning:
πταίω
[in LXX chiefly for נָגַף ni. ;]
1. trans., to cause to stumble (1Ki.4:3, cf. Deiss., BS, 681).
2. Intrans., to stumble. Metaphorical, in moral sense, Rom.11:11, Jas.2:10 3:2, 2Pe.1:10.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: I ask then, did they stumble that they might fall? May it never be! But by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.
For whoever keeps the whole law, and yet stumbles in one point, he has become guilty of all.
Therefore, brothers, be more diligent to make your calling and election sure. For if you do these things, you will never stumble.
